question: Which shader-fetch patch and persistent-cache effects must a draw-entry model distinguish from dropped command words?

scope.boundary: Bounded native-word and narrow generated-code reconciliation. No complete transitive helper-write tree, allocator ownership, runtime model parity or safe draw-consumption result.

dependencies.use: Owns accepted shader selection, copied versus persistent patch destinations and metadata contracts.
Owns the separate dirty-group and bound-state inventory.
Owns the device binding and shader/declaration object field evidence.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only no-analysis queries through tools/run-headless.ps1 using ghidra/DumpFunctions.java, ghidra/DumpInstructions.java and ghidra/DumpMemoryWords.java; narrow exact-function generated corroboration.

inputQualification.claim: A sequential read-only mapped-memory comparison found all differences inside the historical thunk band. None overlaps the cited semantic native windows.
inputQualification.qualification: The mapped program is not byte-identical to the supported flat image. No original thunk semantics or whole-image reader absence follows. Function-body claims rely on source-equivalent inspected words; no repair was performed.

currentEvidence.decompilerLimit: Canonical decompilation truncates at Xenon save/restore thunks or undefined instructions. Sparse decoded iteration can skip gaps; it is not complete function coverage.

drawEntryGate.claim: The draw entry tests low-word mask 0x1E0000 of the dirty qword at G+0x10 before calling 0x826ADD88 with the dirty value. In the big-endian layout this mask is in G+0x14.
drawEntryGate.qualification: This groups four bits. It does not assign each bit the same semantic action.

modeBoundary.claim: The entry masks this bit and conditionally calls 0x826AC6C8. That helper writes derived G+0x2940 and device-byte state plus command words.
modeBoundary.qualification: Complete helper effects and original semantic names remain qualified.

modeBoundary.claim: A shader/fetch update arm can select a persistent variant through 0x826ADC48 or an allocated command copy through 0x826ADA38, with metadata loading through 0x826ADB98.
modeBoundary.qualification: Actual selected variant, cache compatibility, helper returns and allocation remain guarded.

modeBoundary.claim: The bounded generated path includes separate pixel/alternate selection and derived mode state; it is not interchangeable with the stride-triggered patch arm.
modeBoundary.qualification: This is generated corroboration of the native windows, not runtime activation.

modeBoundary.claim: The bit reaches ADD88 through the draw-entry grouped gate. With input exactly0x40000 and no locally added0x80000/0x100000, it skips the0x20000 helper and the0x180000 grouped stores at0x826AE20C/0x826AE21C. A39F8 still clears G+0x10 at0x826A3B44.
modeBoundary.qualification: Other ADD88 mode, binding and command conditions still depend on device state. No independent action was assigned to this bit; do not infer a no-op or map it to0x20000.

transientStrideBoundary.claim: The selected UP lowerer/sink path temporarily stores the low byte of input stride in dwords at G+0x30F0 and can set dirty mask 0x80000 when it differs from the cached stride and a vertex shader is bound.
transientStrideBoundary.qualification: The transient value, restored exit byte, later dirty clears and side-buffer protocol are distinct outputs.

patcherBoundary.claim: The patcher derives three-word, 12-byte fetch-instruction records using shader patch metadata, a 12-byte declaration-record scan and stream stride bytes, orders/canonicalizes scratch records, then copies selected records to codeDestination+12*index.
patcherBoundary.qualification: The guarded byte transformation, table/seed result, scratch ordering and selected 12-byte copy effect are recorded in the byte contract. Actual input/table retention, bounds, aliases and caller resource ownership remain required. This is not a complete host draw model. Ordering and canonicalization write stack scratch.

allocatedCopy.claim: Passes the allocated/copied command-code buffer to 0x826AD150, with VS, declaration, stride bytes and variant supplied separately.
allocatedCopy.qualification: This does not imply that only a disposable copy can be modified. Allocator output and ownership remain unproved.

persistentResource.claim: Can pass the shader resource's selected code address to the same patcher before publishing cache fields.
persistentResource.publication: The selected ADD88 branch appends header0xC0012701, an encoded address derived from the same C+load32(M_v) patched by ADC48, and load32(M_v+4)>>2. It then stamps the selected record. The address encoding is(D&0x1FFFFFFF)+(((rol32(D,12)&0xFFF)+512)&0x1000).
persistentResource.packetInterpretation: External Xenia Type3Opcode identifies0x27 as pointer-based IM_LOAD and0x2B as IM_LOAD_IMMEDIATE: https://github.com/xenia-project/xenia/blob/95a5c3ee250f80c3b9d139658649d9ffb6db3eec/src/xenia/gpu/xenos.h#L1523-L1525 . ADB98's0x2F packet is an ALU-constant load, not the shader-code byte writer.
persistentResource.qualification: The retained code allocation is the published instruction-memory input under that packet/address interpretation. Actual GPU fetch, cache visibility, pointer/variant validity, allocation ownership and fence guards remain unobserved. A CPU reader of the selected patched guest range sees its changed bytes under the byte contract's retention/alias guards.

interiorSite.claim: This is an interior linked-call site for 0x826ADB98, not an independently identified shader-loader entry.

shaderConstructionBoundary.notation: B is the compiled input blob; under retained fields M=load32(B+4), S=load32(B+8). VS and C are the two selected allocation returns.
shaderConstructionBoundary.allocationRequests: CreateVS requests M+40+((load32(B)&1)?832:0) bytes for VS and S bytes separately for C through0x82E29168. The metadata helper call0x8269467C requests0x8281ABB8(VS+872,B,M); call0x826946B0 requests0x827F8550(C,B+M,S).
shaderConstructionBoundary.codePointer: Init receives(VS,C) at0x826946BC and stores C at VS+32 at0x82692B78. This is the retained separate code allocation, not VS itself.
shaderConstructionBoundary.metadata: Init reads offsets at VS+896+8*v. Their producer is the metadata transfer request, corresponding to blob B+24+8*v if that transfer completes as requested. Init does not synthesize this table. It forms M_v=VS+load32(VS+896+8*v)+872 and code=C+load32(M_v).
shaderConstructionBoundary.savedRecords: For selected patch-list word P_i, init copies12 bytes from code+12*(P_i&0xFFF) to VS+68+416*v+12*i when the addresses differ. It stores-1 at VS+40+416*v at0x82692C30; that store is a cache tag, not an offset-table write.
shaderConstructionBoundary.corroboration: Canonical rerevved generated/default/rerevved_recomp.119.cpp:12769-12939 and rerevved_recomp.199.cpp:12503-12648 at observed HEAD81798450751cfb75460269f82c2eb4df02754e80.
shaderConstructionBoundary.qualification: These are allocation/transfer requests and direct pointer/record stores. Hook effects, actual extents, full transfer/alignment behavior, allocator ownership, blob/metadata validity and aliases remain guarded. The existing world-constant transfer evidence also leaves unexpanded0x8281ABB8 alignment branches.

dirtyProducerBoundary.encodingSearch: Aligned initialized mapped words: oris immediates4/8/16 followed within four words by stw+0x14 or std+0x10 using the same result register.29 raw pairs, cap128 not reached; intervening writes and base provenance required confirmation.

producers.condition: Direct render-state setter; also changes G+0x293C bit3 and ORs low-word bit0x200.

SetStreamSource stores stride byte at G+0x30F0+stream. It sets the patch bit when unsigned(stride>>2) is nonzero and differs from the byte at G+0x2E38+stream. This is separate from its caller-mask OR into G+0x18, not a mask transfer.
Selected render-target path with index0, nonnull input object and selected type nibble5/7/15; helper and object validity remain guarded.
Selected initialization path ORs the two bits separately. Its earlier0x82692344 candidate stores to G+0x20 instead.
On the reached hook/count/limit path; complete helper effects remain qualified.
Reached hook-guarded path; earlier0x82698A08 candidate stores to G+0x20 instead.
Reached Resolve path after its helper branch join;0x8269EF2C stores to G+0x20 instead.
Reached clear-quad path after earlier object/mask guards;0x826A27E8 stores to G+0x20 instead.

dirtyProducerBoundary.existingProducers: The runtime-surface evidence owns SetPixelShader0x82692948, SetVertexShader0x82692C48, SetVertexDeclaration0x82692E60 and SetFVF0x826946D8. The UP stride sites remain under transientStrideBoundary.
dirtyProducerBoundary.qualification: This is a bounded producer matrix, not every API or encoding. Remaining0x826B1DA0 candidates exceed this eight-function read set. Computed masks, other distances, indexed/bulk stores, helper aliases and runtime activation remain unproved.

bitActionStoreBoundary.claim: With a live G+0x3198 binding, mode logic can write G+0x2954/+0x2884 and add local dirty bits. The0x100000 arm additionally reaches guarded metadata/cursor and G+0x2928 writes. The0x180000 grouped test at0x826AE1F0..0x826AE1FC gates G+0x2924/+0x2920 stores at0x826AE20C/0x826AE21C.
bitActionStoreBoundary.commandBoundary: Subsequent G+0x2ABC bit0x40, local-mask and record guards select ring append blocks, record stamps and cursor publication. cpuVisibleDeviceWrites/fenceBoundary own their exact stores.
bitActionStoreBoundary.qualification: The direct branch/store frontier does not close metadata, allocation, ring-wrap or other helper effects. It does not assign the0x40000 bit an independent shader operation.

fetchFieldInterpretation.locator: VertexFetchInstruction::Data; bits numbered from each 32-bit word's least significant bit.
fetchFieldInterpretation.word0: Bits20..24 bank,25..26 selector,27..29 prefetch. The reference computes fetch-constant index as3*bank+selector.
fetchFieldInterpretation.word1: Bits0..11 destination swizzle,12 signedness,13 integer/normalization mode,16..21 data format,30 mini-fetch mode.
fetchFieldInterpretation.word2: Bits0..7 dword stride,8..30 signed dword offset.
fetchFieldInterpretation.qualification: External decoder interpretation corroborates the native byte masks; it is not title or hardware proof. The transformation also changes swizzle, signedness, normalization, prefetch and full/mini selection. Sorting moves entire records, so a fixed destination may receive other source-record bits. No opcode validation of every selected input was established; require valid vfetch metadata.

persistentCacheBoundary.claim: The compatibility key is declaration VD+0x30, not the command cursor or a device tag. A zero declaration tag can allocate an ID using global counter 0x82FA0544. The selected record stores a tag at +0x28 and stride qwords at +0x30/+0x38, and the device caches stride state at G+0x2E38/+0x2E40.
persistentCacheBoundary.qualification: A compatible cache hit can reuse code without running the patcher. A busy variant can reject persistent patching. A host model must preserve these distinct branches.

compatibleCacheHitSubmodel.conditions: The selected record's +0x28 tag equals VD+0x30 and the OR of both 64-bit masked stride differences is zero.
compatibleCacheHitSubmodel.outputs: Copy current G+0x30F0 and G+0x30F8 to G+0x2E38 and G+0x2E40, then return r3=1.
compatibleCacheHitSubmodel.qualification: This arm skips the patcher, declaration ID allocation, record tag/stride stores and fence test. It is a limited persistent-output model for this callee, not the complete register/frame contract or a draw-entry consume model.

fenceBoundary.claim: Selected variant records receive current G+0x2A9C at record+0x40 after selected program publication paths. The persistent selector compares this stamp against completion state reached through G+0x2A90.
fenceBoundary.qualification: These are CPU-visible reuse/lifetime inputs. Dropping command words does not alone justify dropping stamps.

cpuVisibleDeviceWrites.claim: Mode, shader selection, shadow-register, byte-flag and cursor stores are distinct from dynamic command-buffer payload words.
cpuVisibleDeviceWrites.qualification: The list is a bounded direct-store result, not all transitive helper writes or an exhaustive reader classification.

dirtyClears.claim: The selected draw body clears dirty qwords at G+0x0,+0x8,+0x10,+0x18,+0x20 after their respective helper paths. A consume's dirty-word policy is a separate model decision, not evidence that native writes are absent.

guards: Do not call the shader update ring-only: persistent shader bytes, declaration tags, variant cache fields and fence stamps can be CPU-visible outputs.
Do not execute a patch on a cache-hit branch that native code reuses without patching.
Do not infer a complete draw-entry model from a one-record patcher formula.
Do not infer actual stream/declaration identity, bounds, lifetime or nonaliasing from compatible shapes.
No full call-tree, allocator, synchronization or runtime parity closure was established.
nextDiscriminators: Bind the actual 0x80000 variant path and its declaration tag, stride masks, completion window and current code destination before selecting a host-model case.
Bind the byte contract's current input/table retention, protected stack and selected code-range guards before admitting a caller case or claiming runtime parity.
Keep zero-tag global-ID allocation, busy-variant fallback, allocation/ring-wrap and unresolved far-helper paths refused until their effects are separately bound.

A separately authorized exit probe must predict without mutating entry state, run Original once, then compare all modeled device/cache/declaration fields and every changed shader byte; classify command-only differences separately.
conclusion: The dirty vertex-fetch path can patch retained shader-code allocation bytes as well as allocated command copies and writes CPU-visible cache, tag, shadow and fence state. A translator using unpatched code and current declaration/stride state is not disproved by those byte differences, but its GPU semantic equivalence and complete guest exit parity remain unproved. Shared-ID allocation, completion, allocator, aliases, metadata validity and helper effects remain qualified; no complete safe consume model is established.
